LINE (Tang et al., 2015) learns separate first-order and second-order proximity embeddings and typically concatenates them into the final node representation, with the embedding treatment depending on edge-sampling optimization. DeepWalk (Perozzi et al., 2014) instead generates truncated random walks over the graph and feeds them to a skip-gram model (word2vec-style) to learn a single node embedding, with settings such as walk length, walks per node, window size, and dimensionality. The common goal is to learn low-dimensional vector representations of network nodes that preserve graph structure and proximity, so they can be used for downstream tasks such as multi-label node classification and link prediction.
